newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN DOLLAR DEPOSITS QUIETLY STEADY IN LATE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DOLLAR DEPOSITS QUIETLY STEADY IN LATE TRADE.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Thursday, dealers said.
Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. weekly jobless claims and June consumer credit data, they said.

Weekly jobless claims for the week ended August 2 are forecast to be around 307,000 compared with 277,000 reported in the previous week. Consumer credit for June is expected to be around US$5.2 billion against May's $3.0 billion.
"Rates were steady to slightly higher in the morning on some position adjustments," a local dealer said.

"Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the weekly jobless claims and consumer credit figures. But I don't think there will be much impact unless the numbers are way off market expectations," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday was unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, weekend rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 and week-fixed was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16, nine-months rose 1/16 point to 5-15/16 5-13/16 and twelve-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent. -- P.Theseira (65-8703085)
